questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language (german), the nature in Austria, the culture, and the distance from Denmark to be able to have visitors.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I had no problems with finding anything. Dagmar Wallenstorfer from International Office at MedUni Graz had organized everything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I found the department I received a lot of documents (maps, folders about the city and more).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
This website was good:
www.wg-gesucht.de

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is good, lived 5 min on bicycle from campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: International Office at MedUniGraz helps with everything

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: E-mail correspondation and then I met up with international office. Very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All the necessary

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fully successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Answer fast on e-mails and you will be fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The 3 departments of my clinical stay showed very different level of teaching. Anaesthesiology was perfect. Neurology okay and gynaecology and obstetrics I would not recommend to anyone.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Not relevant as it was a clinical stay.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Good at anaesthesiology and neurology.
There was no teaching to get at gyn/obs as it was very hierarchi-dominated department. I could only learn from another student who didn't know more than me. The doctors didn't try to teach much.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Clinical rotations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: clinical rotation at anaesthesiology and neurology

questions.answer: Transport was quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot, but as I arrived later I didn't attend to many. But I easily found the other ERASMUS students and enjoyed life.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Bouldering in Newton Boulder Halle is great. A bit expensive. If it's but possible to get a USI course, then please do that. (And register before the day for signing up!!!)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hike in the alps, visit nearby smaller towns and enjoy Styria. Visit Ljubljana (hike there), go to Budapest.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.  Austrian culture is very alike Danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn German. Live in WG with locals - that is very cool. Meet up with your Buddy. Talk to KPJ's (students in last year) at the hospital.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hierarchially old fashioned system at the hospitals is horrible, but not something for you to chance. This was for me very challenging. The tone over for example overweight people is also quite inappropriate.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The humor. The very Austrian language. The friendly greetings of everyone you meet.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Seek all the things you want to learn and go for it. It is important to be very insisting. Visit all the nature spots in the area. If staying more than 3 months then buy the top ticket and travel a lot to the alps.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Graz is walkable, but I would always recommend having a bicycle here.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The experience of living and getting to know another country, culture and another people is so interesting. It was amazing to experience another health care system from the inside and for that I am grateful (even though I complaint a lot about the hierarchy amongst the workers within the system). 
It was amazing learning German with other student from all over Europe and discussing the health care system and the job as a doctor with them. But it was also interesting hearing from all the Austrian health care workers how they experience their own system.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: No in particular challenging episodes/greater challenges arose.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
